Local Moran (LISA)

Source: R/spw.R
lmorn.Rd

Anselin's (1995) local indicator of spatial association for each unit: with z = x - mean(x) and m2 = mean(z^2), I_i = z_i / m2 sum_j w_ij z_j, its expectation and variance under total randomisation, the two-sided normal p-value, and a conditional permutation p-value: unit i keeps its value and its neighbours' values are drawn without replacement from the others, nsim times from seed. The quadrant tells high-high and low-low clusters from high-low and low-high outliers. The p-values are per unit and not adjusted for the many tests made (use stats::p.adjust()); with row-standardised weights the sum of the I_i is S0 times global Moran's I.

Usage

lmorn(x, w, nsim = 0, seed = NULL)

Arguments

x

The values: finite numbers, one per unit.

w

The weights: spwt()'s list, or an spdep listw object, for as many units as x.

nsim

The number of permutations: a whole number from 0.

seed

NULL to draw the simulations' seed from R's generator (so set.seed() fixes them), or one whole number from 0.

Value

A data frame with one row per unit: ii (I_i), e, v, z, p, pperm ((1 + min(#{I* >= I}, #{I* <= I})) / (nsim + 1), NaN without permutations) and quad (1 high-high, 2 low-low, 3 low-high, 4 high-low, 0 neither).

References

Anselin, L. (1995). Local indicators of spatial association: LISA. Geographical Analysis, 27(2), 93-115. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.1995.tb00338.x

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- cbind(x = runif(60), y = runif(60))
v <- ifelse(p[, 1] > 0.7 & p[, 2] > 0.7, 5, 1) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.3)
l <- lmorn(v, spwt(p, k = 5), nsim = 199, seed = 1)
head(l)
#>            ii           e         v          z         p pperm quad
#> 1 -0.08136911 -0.01694915 0.1668323 -0.1577177 0.8746793 0.290    4
#> 2  0.12229676 -0.01694915 0.1668323  0.3409120 0.7331698 0.215    2
#> 3  0.03723394 -0.01694915 0.1668323  0.1326550 0.8944662 0.480    2
#> 4  0.14258312 -0.01694915 0.1668323  0.3905786 0.6961088 0.095    2
#> 5  0.18202573 -0.01694915 0.1668323  0.4871449 0.6261557 0.255    2
#> 6  0.09264972 -0.01694915 0.1668323  0.2683280 0.7884469 0.390    2
